## Cubed-sphere face-state seam sync {#sec-ch03-cslrsync}

### Summary

At a face between two panels, each panel reconstructs the state on its own side from its interior and the state on
the other side from its interpolated ghosts. Without a sync the two panels would solve different Riemann problems for
the same face and the fluxes would not cancel. snapy sends each panel's interior-side state to the neighbour, which
overwrites its ghost-side state with it; then both hold the same pair. Because a panel edge can join two edges of the
same orientation, where one panel's "left" is the other's "right" in the other panel's frame, the two states travel
under keys whose suffix selects the direction, and the receiving block assigns the role in its own frame. A single key without the suffix would swap
the two states at such an edge, and the upwind solver would then pick the downwind state.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The reconstructed left and right states at panel-edge faces are exchanged as raw copies, one face deep,
so both panels solve the same Riemann problem at a shared face; a rule, the suffix rule of the Derivation layer.

**Data.** In/out: the $x_2$ and $x_3$ face states under the keys `*_wl:+` and `*_wr:-`, primitive units.

**Placement.** Inside each stage, after the $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstruction and before the Riemann solves.

**Activation.** No switch; always on with `layout: cubed-sphere`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact copy; one face deep only.

**Evidence.** `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` ($10^{-12}$ relative drift) and
`test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` ($10^{-13}$ drift); both were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

Local symbols: none beyond appendix A, notation group 3, where $q^{\mathrm L}_f, q^{\mathrm R}_f$ are the reconstructed left and right
states of face $f$; the keys `*_wl:+` and `*_wr:-` carry them.

### Derivation

The argument is in `sources/canoe__tracer_seam_TECH_REPORT.md` §4 to §6; it is stated here against the code. In a
block's own frame, at its last face along $+x_2$ the left state $q^{\mathrm L}$ comes from its interior and the right
state $q^{\mathrm R}$ from its ghosts; at its first face the reverse. The pack and unpack rules for a key with a suffix
are:

- a key ending `:+` is sent only toward a direction with no negative offset and received only from a direction with
  no positive offset;
- a key ending `:-` is the mirror image.

The rules are the `suffix` tests in the cross-panel pack ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}) and the
`suffix` tests in the unpack ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}}). With $q^{\mathrm L}$ sent as `hydro_wl:+` and $q^{\mathrm R}$ as
`hydro_wr:-`, a block sends from its last face only $q^{\mathrm L}$, its interior state there, and from its first face
only $q^{\mathrm R}$, again its interior state. A neighbour that lies on the receiver's negative side delivers into the
receiver's $q^{\mathrm L}$; one on its positive side into $q^{\mathrm R}$. Both rules are evaluated in the receiver's
own frame, so at an edge where both panels see the other on their positive side the interior state of the sender lands
in the receiver's $q^{\mathrm R}$, which in the receiver's frame is the side the sender occupies. In every case the
ghost-side state at a shared face is replaced by the neighbour's interior state, and the two blocks hold the same
ordered pair. Nothing is approximated.

### Numerical method

The sync runs inside each stage, after the $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstruction and before the solves. Both directions are
begun, launched and finalised together. The options are `cross_panel_only(true)`, `interpolate(false)` and
`type(kPrimitive)`, with `dim` set to the direction, so only the one face layer at panel edges moves; along $x_1$
the strip also carries the ghost rows of that layer (`extend_x1` by the ghost depth, whenever the block has more than
one $x_1$ cell), because the $x_1$ differences of the face-flux covariance read the cross-panel face states in the
cells next to the radial walls. The velocity frame rotation of @sec-ch03-csinterp is applied to the states, the reverse flag reorders the strip along the
edge, and the flip and transpose flags are no-ops on a strip one face deep. The scalar runs the same sync with
`type(kScalar)` before its own solves. @fig-ch03-cslrsync-roles draws the roles at a same-orientation edge.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "Two cells on either side of a face, each panel's own axis arrow pointing toward the face, with triangles marking the exchanged states."
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

: Code map of the face-state seam sync. {#tbl-ch03-cslrsync-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cslrsync-code):

1. After `precon23` reconstructs the $x_2$ states, the hydro puts them in `send_vars2` under `hydro_wl:+` and
   `hydro_wr:-` and begins the exchange; the same for $x_3$ ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. It launches both and finalises both with `finalize_exchange` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}); the solves
   follow.
3. The scalar does the same with `scalar_wl:+` and `scalar_wr:-` ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** No key: the sync runs whenever `distribute.layout` is `cubed-sphere` and the axis has more than
one cell. It cannot be turned off and refuses nothing. The send and the roles are
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  SyncOptions sync_opts;
  sync_opts.cross_panel_only(true).interpolate(false).type(kPrimitive);
    ...
  if (u.size(DIM2) > 1) {
    wtmp2 = precon23->forward(w, DIM2);

    // sync left/right states across faces for cubed sphere layout
    if (playout->options->type() == "cubed-sphere") {
      send_vars2["hydro_wl:+"] = wtmp2[ILT];
      send_vars2["hydro_wr:-"] = wtmp2[IRT];
      pmb->begin_exchange(send_vars2, sync_opts.dim(DIM2));
    }
  }
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` | six panels with the face-flux covariance on conserve mass, vapour and $\sum_iV_iE_i+\mathrm{PE}_d$ (appendix A, notation group 5; the invariant of cell work with the fixer, as the script states), over the run | $10^{-12}$ relative drift | `DRIFT_TOL` in the script |
| `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` | tracer mass is conserved across seams and the hat stays in $[0,1]$ | $10^{-13}$ drift | `DRIFT_TOL`, @sec-ch03-thetacopy |

: Tests that exercise the face-state sync. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cslrsync-tests}

The conservation arm is `arm_conservation` ({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py arm_conservation >}}) and
its threshold `DRIFT_TOL` ({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DRIFT_TOL >}}); a shared face whose two panels
solved different problems would leak and fail it. There is no dedicated C++ unit test of the suffix rule itself. The tests run
on CPU in one process. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).


The suffix rule itself is checked by enumeration: for the four pairings of the face's side in the sender and in the
receiver, including the two same-orientation edges, the pack and unpack tests move exactly one state, the sender's
interior-side one, into the receiver's ghost-side slot (`[C20]`).[^cslr-c20]

[^cslr-c20]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, line `[C20]`; a Python port of the suffix tests of
    `CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize` and `CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize` with their positional payload at the
    pin; CPU; Python and sympy as in the other footnotes of this chapter.

### Limits

No known limits. The transpose and flip flags are computed for these strips but have no effect on a strip one face
deep (read from the code). The suffix rule has the Python enumeration above but no direct C++ unit test (not measured). The switch combinations that are
tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
